title: Government Cloud Policy, The Gambia
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy, Republic of The Gambia
why_not: Fetched and staged, but selected as the baseline for data localisation policies, not for this indicator. The Government Cloud Strategy 2023-2027, already staged on 2026-09-02, is the strategy this indicator asks for; the Cloud Policy is its companion governance instrument and is also unsigned, its Issue Date and Effective Date left as placeholders.

title: GRA Boss Urges Gambians to Embrace Digital Transformation
why_not: Fetched and not staged. It confirms the National Enterprise Architecture validation workshop, organised by GICTA with the ITU and GovStack, but it is a second report of an event whose primary report is already held in the base (DUP-EXACT on the TechReviewAfrica article), and its body is substantially about Gambia Revenue Authority revenue digitalisation rather than the architecture. Staging it would spend ingest effort on a duplicate event and would not move the indicator.

title: Information and Communications Act, 2009
publisher: Government of The Gambia (via WIPO Lex)
why_not: Not fetched. Domestic ICT statute, not a regional-harmonisation instrument, and the ministry's Malabo Convention record already held the baseline. Reported as under review since 2022, so operative status is uncertain.

title: ECOWAS Legal Text / legal journal index
why_not: Not fetched. An undated index of ECOWAS Supplementary Acts, not a Gambia-specific document; listing an instrument does not evidence Gambian domestication.

title: Protocol to the Agreement Establishing the AfCFTA on Digital Trade
why_not: Not fetched. Continental instrument with no Gambia-specific signature or ratification entry on the page, so it establishes nothing about The Gambia's position.

title: National Assembly passes Personal Data Protection and Privacy Bill, 2025
why_not: Not fetched. Cap filled by two stronger items. A specialist secondary report of domestic legislation; the National Assembly is the primary and the event is domestic law rather than regional harmonisation.

title: Information and Communication Technical Committee Meeting on ECOWAS Harmonization Standards
why_not: Not fetched. Out of the progress window and weaker than the catalogue as a baseline; reports standards under consideration for adoption rather than adopted.

title: CATALOGUE OF THE GAMBIA STANDARDS BUREAU 2022
why_not: Fetched and staged, but as the baseline for national quality standards. Its GAMS ISO, GAMS IEC and GAMS CODEX designations are strong evidence here too; the ISO member profile was preferred as this indicator's baseline to avoid one document holding two baselines.

title: Information and Communication Technical Committee Meeting on ECOWAS Harmonization Standards
why_not: Not fetched. Lists ISO/IEC 27001, 27002, 27032, 29100, 27701 and ISO 10008 as candidates for national adoption, i.e. consideration not completed adoption, and predates the window.

title: Cyberwellness Profile - The Gambia
why_not: Not fetched. Superseded: a 2011 negative finding about cybersecurity standards, contradicted by TGSB's later work. Operative beats superseded.

title: Stakeholders in The Gambia review of the draft new legal and regulatory framework to govern the digital economy in West Africa
why_not: Not fetched. Names Gambian non-government participants well but is a 2022 event report, and the WARDIP SEP was preferred as the baseline because it is the standing instrument.

title: Validation Workshop for the National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy, The Gambia
why_not: Not fetched. Out of the progress window and a weaker baseline than the SEP. Held in reserve if the window is ever widened.

title: Accelerating Digital Transformation in West Africa
why_not: Not fetched. News of the agreement rather than the agreement; the Financing Agreement itself was staged instead.

publisher: Office of the President, The Gambia

title: Individuals using the Internet
why_not: The authoritative international series, latest Gambian observation 2024, but the page is a dynamic query interface that exposes no numeric value in static HTML and yields no document body to capture verbatim. title: Measuring digital development: The affordability of ICT services 2024
why_not: Correct baseline for this indicator and already held by OSINT: raw-url-index returned DUP-EXACT against raw/2025/2025-01-01-itu-measuring-digital-development-affordability-of-ict-services-2024.md. why_not: Landing page for the ICT price basket collection, not a publication of a Gambian value. No country figure to capture.

title: Telecommunications Tariff
why_not: The regulator's own tariff record, but it carries local call and SMS rates only and no mobile data prices at all, and it is dated 2021. title: GRA to track telecom revenues in push for transparency
why_not: Telecom Revenue Assurance System for GRA visibility over telecom transactions. Tax administration of existing VAT and excise, not a change to consumer prices or to any affordability measure; ranked third by the agent and below the cap.

title: Gambia data (international bandwidth per Internet user)
why_not: The internationally comparable used-capacity-per-user series, but the same dynamic interface problem: no static value and no document body to capture.

title: The Gambia Submarine Cable (GSC)

title: PURA explains frequent fibre cuts and plans to explore securing second fibre cable and extra backup facilities
why_not: Strong regulatory account of ACE dependence, repeated cuts and mandated Sonatel backup, but dated January 2022: out of the progress window and weaker than the Gamtel profile as a statement of current capacity.

publisher: Tender Impulse (republishing a World Bank-sourced notice)
why_not: Dropped on origin: origin-screen returns DROP for tenderimpulse.com as an excerpt aggregator republishing third-party government tender notices behind its own listing pages. The underlying GSC 2.0 procurement notice would be admissible from its own publisher; this listing is not.

title: Serekunda Internet Exchange Point
why_not: Independent registry confirming SIXP as Active, established 25 July 2013, Ethernet, subnet 196.223.34.0/24. Fetched, but its subnet, facility, contact and participant tables are all empty, so it corroborates existence and adds no operating detail the exchange's own page lacks.

title: SIXP membership
why_not: Membership and governance rules from the same undated site as the selected about page, which already carries the membership rule. Second page of one document rather than a second document.

title: SIXP Gambia
why_not: The only quantitative peering snapshot located: 1 Gbit/s capacity, two open peers, three connections, ASN 37698. Last updated March 2020, so it cannot establish the present state; its figures are recorded in the selected baseline file note instead.

title: SIXP (Serrekunda IXP)
why_not: Offered against the progress brief but last updated 2019, so it evidences no movement inside the window. Brief 2 returned no qualifying dated IXP development at all, which is the finding for this indicator.

title: The Gambia Government Cloud Policy
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy
why_not: Makes backup, restoration, business continuity and disaster recovery explicit requirements of cloud service descriptions and SLAs, and assigns GICTA the government-cloud role. A requirement on future services, not a record of capacity that exists; the Cloud Strategy holds the facility inventory and took the baseline slot.

title: Government Cloud Implementation Plan
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy
why_not: Treats consolidation, National Data Centre upgrade, resilience and disaster recovery as work still to be scoped. Third in rank and below the single baseline cap.

title: Barrow Inaugurates National Data Centre, Digital Identity System
why_not: The clearest in-window data-storage movement, and already held by OSINT: raw-url-index returned DUP-EXACT against raw/2026/2026-07-01-barrow-inaugurates-national-data-centre-nims-standard.md. Dropped as already-seen, which is why this indicator stages no progress item; the evidence is in the base already.

title: Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), WARDIP The Gambia
publisher: Government of The Gambia under World Bank environmental and social requirements
why_not: Safeguards framework for planned GAMTEL/GAMCEL data-centre works; considers data-centre energy consumption and generator impacts but certifies no facility power, water or cooling adequacy. Supporting, not conclusive, and below the single baseline cap.

title: The Gambia Electricity Sector Roadmap 2021-2040
publisher: Ministry of Petroleum and Energy / NAWEC
why_not: Official system-level assessment recording the gap between installed and available generation capacity, so it is relevant context for data-centre power resilience, but it assesses the national system and not any data centre, and it says nothing about cooling or water. Ranked third and below the single baseline cap, which the Government Cloud Strategy took as the only document testing adequacy at facility level.

title: Nawec Explains Current Power Crisis Linked To Iran War
why_not: Same NAWEC press conference and the same 106 MW peak against 78 MW available as the already-staged The Point report of 8 April 2026. Dropped as duplicate-in-run: a second report of one event, which is the commonest way the cap gets wasted.

title: The Gambia Electricity Sector Roadmap 2021-2040
publisher: Ministry of Petroleum and Energy / NAWEC
why_not: The cabinet-level masterplan for universal access and the Eastern Backbone, but its access baseline predates the 2024 figure carried by the selected National Energy Compact, which supersedes it on the number this indicator turns on.

title: Stakeholder Engagement Plan for the WA-REMP Phase 2
why_not: Reports roughly 74 per cent access in 2024 and identifies remaining unelectrified communities, but it is a project safeguards and engagement document rather than a national statement of position, and its figure duplicates the Compact's.

title: E-GOVERNMENT STRATEGY 2021-2024
publisher: Ministry of Information and Communication Infrastructure
why_not: Describes fragmented, ministry-specific systems and limited centralised databases, so it bears on robustness, but it is older and less asset-specific than the Cloud Strategy stocktake. Staged once and selected as the baseline for the local-capacity indicator instead; one file, one selection each.

title: Gambia ICT Agency Act, 2019
publisher: Government of The Gambia / National Assembly
why_not: The statute establishing GICTA with responsibility for government ICT standards, procurement specifications, maintenance, security and ICT audit. It establishes the governance instrument, not the condition or age of the equipment, which is what this indicator asks.

title: GAMTEL, SYSROAD sign $50M PPP to modernise Gambia's broadband network
why_not: Offered by the agent against this indicator, but it concerns the national telecommunications backbone rather than government hardware and software. Staged once under international internet bandwidth and not counted here; the cap is a maximum and this indicator stages no progress rather than take a poor fit.

title: Barrow Inaugurates National Data Centre, Digital Identity System
why_not: The strongest in-window movement offered for this indicator, the NIMS/GAM ID biometric identity platform on new data-centre infrastructure, and already held by OSINT: raw-url-index returned DUP-EXACT against raw/2026/2026-07-01-barrow-inaugurates-national-data-centre-nims-standard.md. Dropped as already-seen, which is why this indicator stages no progress item.

title: Government Cloud Strategy 2023-2027
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy
why_not: Identifies gaps in government IT skills, capabilities and institutional knowledge and records GICTA as established but not yet operational at the time of assessment. Ranked second here behind the e-Government Strategy, which is the dedicated capacity assessment; already staged from 2026-09-02 in any case.

title: Gambia ICT Agency Act, 2019
publisher: Government of The Gambia / National Assembly
why_not: Assigns GICTA first-level technical support, centralised data-centre facilities, systems development, training and management of government ICT employees. Proves the mechanism exists; says nothing about staffing levels or actual capability, and below the single baseline cap.

title: FIRST-PURA (gmCSIRT) Cybersecurity Hands-on Training for Critical National Infrastructure staff
publisher: The Gambia Computer Security Incident Response Team (gmCSIRT)
why_not: A third distinct in-window training event, 27-30 April 2026, covering ransomware response, forensics and a cyber drill for CNI technical staff. Genuine and admissible, but third past a two-progress cap; recorded here so widening the cap needs no new agent_run.

title: Government Cloud Policy
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy
why_not: Ranked below the E-Government Strategy and not fetched by this slice. Assigns the future Government Cloud a role in interoperable services but describes the architecture as an objective to be operationalised; the agent reports its text carries an issue date to be inserted. Already staged by a sibling slice.

title: Government Cloud Strategy 2023 - 2027
publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy
why_not: Already staged in new-queue on 2026-09-02 carrying dpi.exchange in its topics, so available without restaging. Not selected as baseline: it frames cloud and a digital marketplace as the means to enable integration and records that interoperability standards were not yet adopted, weaker on the exchange layer than the E-Government Strategy.

title: Implementation Status & Results Report: The Gambia Essential Health Services Strengthening Project (P173287), ISR03661
why_not: Fetched. Strong dated status: electronic case-based surveillance developed and integrated into DHIS2 and marked Achieved, eHRMIS and eLMIS established, eCRVS interoperability with other MIS recorded as being established and on track. Excluded only by the one-baseline cap. Archived 12 May 2025, so out of window for the progress brief.

title: National Health Policy 2021-2030
why_not: Not fetched; ranked third. Sets the objective of a robust integrated health information system and a harmonised data warehouse and records the absence of robust EMR, laboratory and integrated HR systems, but states an intended architecture rather than what interoperates.

title: The Gambia Annual Report 2022
why_not: Not fetched; ranked fourth. Corroborating only: records DHIS2 reporting support and continuing fragmentation of health information systems. Date unverified by this run.

title: 2026 Programme Based Budget Book, Executive Budget Proposal
publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs
why_not: Not fetched. The agent discounted its DHIS2 and e-LMIS references as routine budget line items rather than a new interoperability deployment; the 2026 Budget Speech from the same ministry was taken instead.

title: The Gambia - DHIS2
publisher: DHIS2 / HISP with the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education
why_not: Fetched. More current than the selected use case and confirms national scale since 2019, the SEMIS App for individual data and the 2021 individual student identification number, but it is a programme implementation page that never addresses whether EMIS connects to WAEC, HR or other government systems. Excluded by the one-baseline cap.

title: Combined Project Information Documents: The Gambia Education Sector Support Program (P162890)
why_not: Fetched as batch ballast. Records that EMIS required further development to link MoBSE and MoHERST, which was not then captured, and distinguishes WAEC assessment responsibility from ministry EMIS functions. Excluded by the cap and eight years stale as a current position.

title: Data Use Innovations for Education Management Information Systems in The Gambia, Uganda, and Togo
why_not: Not fetched. A multi-country project page whose Gambia-specific content does not establish interoperability with legacy HR or WAEC systems; ranked below the country use case and the implementation page.

title: Implementation Completion and Results Report: The Gambia Social Safety Net Project (P167260)
why_not: Fetched as part of a batch. Establishes GamSR was institutionalised and used at closing by six programmes and actors including Nafa, NDMA, ROOTS, CRS and WFP, which is programme-level data reuse rather than registry-to-registry interoperability. Excluded by the one-baseline cap in favour of the founding design framework.

title: The official Website of Gambia Immigration Department
why_not: Fetched. Confirms GID issues national identity cards, passports, visas and residence permits and runs border control, but carries no date, no coverage or enrolment figure and no technical detail. Its news headlines render as unreadable placeholder characters and its Policies and Strategies and ICT Sector Statistics blocks are an unrelated ICT-ministry template showing zeros, so the page is partly boilerplate. Too thin to serve as a baseline on robustness.

title: Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 11 of 1886, as amended to 1974 (Cap. 41:01)
why_not: Not fetched. The governing civil-registration statute, but it predates digital identity entirely and creates no unique identifier or digital credential at birth, so it cannot establish this indicator's subject. Retained because it remains the legal instrument a later pass may want.

title: Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 11 of 1886, as amended to 1974 (Cap. 41:01)
why_not: Not fetched. Establishes the legal registration function but contains no interoperability or identifier-linkage architecture, which is precisely why it does not answer this indicator.

title: CRVS - Birth, Marriage and Death Registration in Gambia
why_not: Not fetched. Country profile giving the legal and institutional CRVS baseline and birth-registration completeness, but it predates the eCRVS deployment and the identity linkage this indicator asks about by five years.

title: Financial Inclusion (National Financial Inclusion Strategy working document)
why_not: Fetched. Contains one relevant line, that the national biometric identification card being issued will support Know Your Customer requirements, but it is future tense and the document carries no title page, no publication date and no author; its only internal timeline runs to June 2020. Too weak and too poorly identified to stage as a baseline.

title: Why & How do I register?
why_not: Not fetched. Establishes that a passport, national identity card, birth certificate or attestation may be used as identity evidence for voter registration, which is documentary acceptance rather than automated use of the identity database. Undated web page.

publisher: Parliament of The Gambia (text hosted by CBG)

Staging it would put a citable but unreadable text behind a governance finding.

publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs, Republic of The Gambia

publisher: Ministry of Health, Republic of The Gambia

publisher: Attorney General's Chambers and Ministry of Justice; UNDP-managed procurement
